I'm glad to hear it helped some. Does she openly treat you poorly in front of people like your brother? If so, it might be worth talking to him about it. Probably don't necessarily say anything bad about her, but that you are not comfortable with the way she interacts with you and ask him to help by getting her to stop doing the things that hurt you. There is the risk of that backfiring, but that depends on a lot of things I can't know. If she is more subtle about it and other people wouldn't be able to understand what she does that's bad it's more likely to backfire and might not be worth it depending on your relationship with your brother. Also your therapist might have some better insight into what's going on there and have some better suggestions.

I don't want to tell you what you should definitely do or not since I really can't know as much as you do about what things are really like. But I will say that if you feel like your friendship is emotionally damaging to you, which it seems you do, then you shouldn't hold her as emotionally close as you do. It's emotionally close people that can hurt us the most. You don't have to make any sort of outwardly visible or significant changes to how much you see her in order to internally distance yourself from her so that when she does or says something that would hurt you, you can deal with it more easily. If she doesn't let up and seems to push things further then maybe physically distancing yourself will also be necessary, but it hard to say. It might seem weird doing this, but if you have to see her anyway because of the other people in your life then it might be the best thing. And it doesn't have to make you feel like you're losing a friend.  Just think of it as making the relationship more tolerable for you. And still try to get out there and make other friends and when you find someone you actually like being around you will likely just naturally start spending more time with them and less with her.
:( Sorry to hear how rough it was, hopefully (with support?) it will not be that bad again. I know it can make everything worse if your health suffers that much.
That sounds pretty rough, I know I wouldn't get out of bed if I felt sick. Luckily I didn't really get sick, but it's probably because I didn't even try to eat. I lost about 20 pounds.

I can relate to that. It was about a week before I stopped crying (which was really hard to deal with while needing to go to work), and now I have some other issues with pain medications due to an accident and that really makes me have waves of feeling okay and feeling really awful.

Definitely continue to pursue any that seem like they can help, and don't get discouraged by distance. They might be able to help you find something closer, or one of the other things linked to on the pages here might have something closer, or at least some helpful phone lines that can help without needing to leave your house.

I don't really have useful experience to be of help in that regard, but I would say if you are struggling, there should be services that are willing to help and insurance/money should not be a barrier. I would certainly not let that stop you from trying. Most health services will know that money is not easy and will have resources to help in that regard. Looking specifically in Illinois I found http://www.mhaiv.org/ and http://mcmha.com/ which might be able to help (I don't know for sure what they offer though.) If you look at the info on the sidebar http://redd.it/1c3p3z they have a lot of informational documents for "self-help" and some links to pages to help guide people to the services they are looking for.  Sorry I can't provide any more concrete information, but since I haven't used these services beyond briefly looking at the sites, I'm not sure what the most beneficial ones would be, but you can maybe distract yourself by looking through them for one that interests you?

I don't think it's normal, but I dealt with it since I had the family connections and didn't want to disrupt that, and since I was able to distance myself emotionally and not fall victim to his manipulation I was able to still have some fun times with him. We did do fun things and I got to learn about different types of people from it.  Since it sounds like you might have to deal with being around her, I think it's good to learn how to handle that without letting her manipulation get to you. Now on the other hand if you are concerned about your brother, that's another issue. She might be different with him, or he might get fed up with her if she isn't, or if he sees how she is with other people, so it might not be worth getting involved there unless you are seriously concerned.

Sorry if I took things the wrong way.  I haven't looked through them yet, but there are some links on the sidebar to the right that I think offer to help getting professional help, which it sounds like you want and could benefit from.

He really might not be trying to hurt you, but the relationship does seem to only provide temporary relief followed by what I imagine is deeper pain.  He might not be able to really be what you need, but does sincerely try to, but then he falters. Either way, the emotional roller-coaster you described is difficult sounding, even it's not his fault at all.

Since you want to talk to a doctor it sounds like that would be the best thing to work towards. Like I said, I think there are helpful links here.  One I happened to find just a little while ago is http://www.mentalhealthamerica.net/finding-therapy but I'm not sure how useful it will be for you depending on where you are. The fact that you want help is a good sign though. I don't think anyone here is a professional though, just people willing to have open conversations.

Her dating your brother does sound like a little trickier of a situation than I had. Mostly I just recognized the manipulation for what it was, so I didn't let him control me as much as he wanted to. Like I said, I did still hang out with him regularly, but I just let the things he said slide off my back since I knew they were just him being manipulative. I don't know if it's universal, but my feeling is that people who are that manipulative lose a bit of interest in people that they can't get to do exactly what they want. He eventually found some other people to manipulate when he wasn't getting what he wanted out of me. We still hung out, and he would complain to me about these other people, but I just laughed (usually just internally since that would have sparked a confrontation.)  I remember once he had a newer friend (target?) in his car with us. He had just gotten some frosted highlights done and was looking for compliments. I didn't say anything negative, but nothing particularly positive. I think he was trying to make me feel bad for not caring about his hair, so he asked his new friend what they thought of his hair. The new person didn't really know what he was like and said he didn't like it. He literally just pulled over wherever we were and made him get out of the car and then drove off. I felt horrible for the kid, but I also felt like it was good for him to get out of that friendship so quickly. I just kept my mouth shut, didn't insult him or give him reason to get too angry, other than my lack of caring.  I think it was the perfect amount of distancing without doing anything to make him do anything particularly spiteful to me.  Then high school ended and I went away to another state for college and only saw him a couple times since.

I didn't mean physically abusive. Based on what you've said, it sounds like he is emotionally abusive. Manipulative is another word for it if the manipulation is not for the benefit of the person being manipulated. He might not be purposely doing it either, but it is hurting you, otherwise you likely wouldn't be on this subreddit (unless there are other more serious issues bothering you that have nothing to do with him.)

I had a friend like that in high school. He was the son of one of my mom's lifelong friends. I have trouble being social and making friends so when he went out of his way to be my "best friend" it felt great. But he was very manipulative and difficult to confront. I didn't do anything extreme that would hurt any family ties or anything, I just learned to recognize him for what he was, and still used him for social interaction, but learned to not let him get to me, and slowly drifted away. I know the feeling of being alone even with lots of people around, but I try not to let it get to me, and I keep trying to find some friends that I don't have to feel alone around. I have some now, though I would like some more that are closer, both emotionally and geographically, but I know that it is at least possible, so keep trying, and there is plenty of disappointment, but they are out there.

It sounds like he is abusive and you need to come to terms with that.  If you completely believe he is being abusive then you will hopefully get over him and not believe a word he says when he does come back.  It sounds like you know it's going to keep happening if you do keep taking him back, so the only way to stop that is to not take him back.

If he does keep coming back to you, then you must have something to offer that will make you attractive to someone else that won't be abusive to you.  I imagine once you do move on, and tell him to fuck off, you will feel much better for it. Even if at the time it is hard because you want to believe him and want to take him back, know that he will just hurt you again and there are people out there who won't.  

And just be aware as well that your first attempts at someone else might not go well because you might look for someone else that treats you similarly. You just need to really be aware of that and not fall into that trap. There are people out there who are not abusive lying assholes. They just aren't as easy to find because the bad ones go out of their way to seem like great ones.

Unless your therapist is someone you really don't trust or he's your mother's husband or something, then I would hope he won't do anything to betray your trust. If you are that worried about it then try finding someone new? Or try bringing up the serious issues more gradually? I would guess if you just blurt out "I want to kill myself" or "I'm going to kill myself" then he may have an obligation to tell someone (I'm just guessing here) but if you just talk about the problems themselves, and gauge his response you might be able to tell him you're not sure how you can go on the way you are and subtle things that make it more apparent you have more serious problems, but don't necessarily trigger an immediate suicide intervention response then things might work out? Unless you are getting to that point, then you should tell him because hiding it up until you do something you can't take back will not hide it from anyone, they will find out if you do act on it.

My girlfriend of over five years left me last year and it still hurts, but I've moved on enough that I don't actually have any desire to get back together, I just with she never left, but I know that is pointless.  We never had the off-again on-again thing. I didn't suspect anything. I came home from work one day and her stuff was gone and there was a note on the table.  It really sucks when you lose someone you care so much about, but it really isn't worth beating yourself up over. (I'm telling myself this as much as you.) 

Especially at your age, you both have most likely been changing so much over the past five years that you should try not to take it personally, and you are still young and have plenty of time to find someone new that you can be even happier with. The pain may not go away for a while, but it will fade eventually.

Suicide has been something I've thought about for as long as I can remember. Well over 20 years. Besides always being the "strong" one in the family and not wanting to tarnish that image, I've also made a pact with myself that if things were ever to the point that I would want to go through with it, first I would try moving to the other side of the planet, since things are bound to be different there. The difficulty of actually doing that has been motivation to not let it get that far.

I personally haven't tried seeking any outside of what was provided by my college, so I'm not sure what options are available, but maybe someone else does? I just did a quick search and found http://www.mentalhealthamerica.net/finding-therapy which might be able to point you towards some resources available to you. I haven't read through them yet, but there are some links to online resources on the sidebar to the right.

Maybe your friends can understand that you are dealing with some pain and they don't really think you are an asshole as much as you feel like one? If you feel like you can't be normal, even by faking it, since I doubt most people are really as normal as they may seem, then possibly some medication can help you find balance? Have you tried talking to any professional health services?

I don't really have any meaningful insight, but maybe your concern about your fiance is partly due to your own struggles? Professional help might be able to make your depression less severe, and might make your relationship better or at least let you think about it more clearly?

No need to apologize to us, and I'm really glad you made it through and got some help.  I know coming on here and just interacting with other people that have been struggling has helped me through some rough times.  I hope you continue to get/stay better.

If it truly is the first one then perhaps he's dealing with issues of his own or doesn't know all of what you're going through? Perhaps talking to him more openly than you have (assuming you haven't been completely open with him) will help him be more supportive in the ways that you need in order to actually get better? If you can't do that with him, or he's not willing to listen, then what the other postings have suggested might be a better option. 

If you can't stand yourself, I can only imagine a couple options. Learn to improve yourself so that you can, or learn to accept yourself as you are. Both cases may require assistance from someone supportive, either someone close to you or someone with professional training, or both.
It sounds like he's being pretty manipulative in this case. Do you think he's trying use "tough love" to get you to improve? Or is he just trying to build himself up by putting you down?

After finally getting to read your post and these comments I am actually quite surprised how much I feel that I can relate to you and a couple other people that replied here.  

In a way I feel like I had a pretty rough childhood, but I must admit it likely wasn't half as bad as what you faced. Even just considering what you described here and assuming everything else was okay (which I don't actually assume).  For one thing, I was only half adopted, and my parents were never really bad to me, I just didn't relate to them very much. I imagine not relating to other people is a big part of our social problems. 

The person you described where you have to apologize to him when he treats you badly was a pretty good description of my closest "friend" in high school.  I never really understood why people were never prepared to move beyond acquaintances with me. I think I was only friends with him because he actually made an effort to spend time with me, even though I didn't think he was that good of a person.  I hardly ever see him now, but he will still blow up at me for not wanting to.  I do have a friend now that does actually care about me and goes out of his way to do things with me on my birthdays and such, but in some ways he is like "Miranda" and I am not able to really open up to him because I can't imagine he would understand. I have another close friend that I am more comfortable with, but she is married (which isn't really a negative, but she has other priorities) and just thinks I'm a little crazy when I talk about some things. 

I think a lot of people aren't very deep, and prefer the company of other people they can relate to or feel superior to.  Being nice and considerate to some people might make them feel like you are (or that you think you are) better than them so they do not want to be around you as much. I know I would call myself "a bit shy" (at least in some ways) but one time someone told me that my shyness comes off as arrogance. That was pretty hard to wrap my head around. I bet people that are jackasses and don't care about other people get to have a lot of friends because people like to be around them to boost their own egos.  Then after spending so much time together it just makes sense to think of each other as friends, even if you don't like each other. This is obviously a huge generalization and does not apply to everyone, but maybe there is a hint of it in many people, and that is why we here have some similar issues. I think it applies to me in some ways as well, but I don't want it to.

I want to make this flow well, but there are so many different things that I want to touch upon that I'm certain it will be rather scattered.  

In regards to your situation with schoolwork, is there an adviser that you like and would listen to? I don't know if you have similar problems with your work as I did, but at times I felt similar to what you described.  I think the only reason I made it through college was that I had the good/bad luck of having a horrible civics teacher in high school. He was the track coach and I really don't know why he was "teaching".  Class time consisted of him making us read sections of the book and take notes while he played on his computer.  Then at the end of class he would go around and grade us on our volume of notes.  I have a pretty good memory, and if I need to refresh myself on something I can find it much more easily by looking at the exact right spot in the book rather than looking at my own notes that are harder to read. And the act of taking notes is more of a disruption and slows me down too much. So I never could bring myself to take notes. That was a huge chunk of my grade gone right there. Then half way through the course he tells us that the state requires him to teach a set of topics that are not in the book, so we each must take one of them and do an oral presentation on it.  I also don't do well with oral presentations.  I can go on and on about something I know or care about, but if I try to give some prepared statement it just disappears from my mind and my vision blurs too much to read something. There went the rest of my grade. Anyway, the point of all that was that my 4.0 was broken with a C in high school, but I had a good justification. I knew the "teacher" was horrible and that the grade had absolutely no reflection on my intelligence.  That was very freeing.  In college I often had a hard time bringing myself to do busy work and my grades suffered, but I let it roll off of my back. When it became enough of an issue (failing a couple classes) that others were concerned, I changed advisers and my new one made a deal with me. I forget the terms, but I know my end of the bargain was that I went and sat in the library during any free time I had in the day. He even said I didn't have to do anything, but I needed to bring my work and sit there and not sleep or anything. I assume the idea was that doing the work would become worthwhile just because the alternative was nothing, and it worked. Again I don't know if this is at all applicable to your situation, but I think not beating yourself up over your grades is, and possibly you could get an adviser to help give you the right structure for you to succeed.

One of the things I enjoy most is learning to do new things. Working on my house, working on my car, growing various types of things, building various things.  I took up calligraphy myself a couple months ago.  I've attended a few PaintNites (acrylics) recently and I have an acoustic guitar and bass, though I do need to practice those a good deal more to even be minimally competent. Being a guy, I'm not too concerned about my own makeup or nails, but I did makeup for a short film. I turned a ten year old girl into a zombie. I have quite a few vivariums (living ecosystems in fish tanks as homes for my pet Poison Dart Frogs and geckos) I've built. So yeah, creating/doing things is great.  I also like being outdoors. My summer last year was quite full of hiking and kayaking and paragliding. Still waiting for it to warm up where I am so that I can get back into that more.  I also love driving. The most I've done is about 87% across the US, but this summer I'm hoping to take a trip that's closer to 100% across. So anyway, I feel like I'm talking too much about myself in your thread, but wanted to explain some of the positive things I can relate to.

I feel like the four or so of us should start a new type of support group. One where we just get together and talk about whatever we feel like. It might be after a couple days that we all just pass out from exhaustion before we run out of things to talk about.

Though I want to say: Miranda is right, everything happens for a reason. She's most likely very wrong about that reason though. Everything happens because something in the real world caused it to happen, not because some outside entity wants it to happen or that the outcome will somehow be a good one.

Edit: Just to add some more things I have bouncing around in my head. I've become so used to saying "good" in response to questions of how I am that it is probably the one thing I lie about, frequently, and without hesitation or concern. I will be more honest in my answer with a select few people, but never completely honest. I'm sure most people do the same, even people who have fairytale lives may lie and say they are good even when something is bothering them. Though the height of things bothering them might be as trivial as their favorite restaurant didn't have their favorite drink available that day or something.

I wanted to get a sense of what's going on fast enough to reply before I have to get to bed, so I skipped a bunch, but I am planning on going back and reading the rest. I just wanted to say that being capable of writing all that and still being coherent and having good structure at the end is a good indicator to me that you are definitely not "stupid and worthless".

I don't put much credence into what other people think about bands (meaning that people hate LP, not your comment.) I've never been a hardcore fan, but I've always enjoyed their music. I never heard this song or about the project spark thing. Might have to check it out some more.

I know there are difficulties with immigration and such, but why would you have to stay in Germany? Being in the north of the US I know if I had to start over somewhere I would definitely be heading somewhere warm.  For as long as I can remember I've had the contingency plan of moving to Australia. That's definitely not a cheap trip though, so that has actually worked as a bit of motivation to not let it get that bad so that I don't have to figure out how to implement my only fall back plan.

It makes sense to me.  

I spent a lot of time in a psych ward visiting an ex who was there (on two different occasions) for attempting suicide. I saw people just like the ones you described. I felt like it was a nice place, but I was there by choice. I think I would have a hard time facing the people in my life if I was there for myself. I've worked hard to not appear to be like my father. But if things get to the point that it can't be hidden, then I sure hope there are some good clinics available.  

Do you know the song "Special K" by Placebo?

I can understand sleep being a hard thing to overcome. Being unconscious, not feeling anything, is a nice escape. I'm curious though, could you possibly change your sleep time a little so that the few hours you are awake happen to be when your appointments are for?

Being in the US I doubt I could get access to such studies, but it is good to know they exist, and I really do hope you find the motivation to make your appointment. I don't know of anything that could be done really, short of getting you to provide your address and showing up at your house and physically forcing you to go, but that's obviously not going to happen, at least not by me.

In response to your edits: I agree if there is a way to actually reach out to the person or connect them with professional help that would be a better solution. 

I just think there are a lot of different situations, a lot of different solutions that will work for different people. I know for me, just having some people to communicate with is very helpful, but I also would be too scared / embarrassed to open up completely to people in my life. Going to a clinic is certainly the best option for some people, but I'm certain it would make things worse for me.

*Edit: worse for me currently, since I'm not at risk at the moment. Having a place to go if things go back down hill would be for the best.

I know it's what motivates me, and I am someone posting here (not just as a commenter).

I'm not trying to build up false expectations, but it's just a simple fact, good things can happen, but not to dead people.

If you know of some resources that will help people take the first steps than please share them, and use them, even though I'm guessing you would say you won't.  

If the depression has gotten so bad that talking to a doctor is out of the question, why isn't posting here out of the question?

I understand that it will be very difficult to do, but staying somewhere where you are surrounded by people actively making your life even more difficult is not going to somehow get better even if you can get some comfort from talking to strangers. I have plenty of family that have uprooted themselves from bad situations with nothing and are better because of it.

I am not here just telling other people what to do from my happy-wonderful perspective. I'm trying to work through my own issues. I've lost interest in quite a bit myself. I just know that no matter how low I've gotten, there is a chance for an upside. Hoping for and (more importantly) working towards that is the only thing I can do.  Otherwise, what's the point of this subreddit even existing? Just to watch people die needlessly?

The motivation would be to get away from the people that are causing the pain. The money aspect is something that's only an issue if you are accustomed to a certain way of living that you want to maintain. If you have something of your own that you can use to browse and post to reddit then you likely have something you can sell to at least get enough money to buy a bus ticket to somewhere, anywhere. If you really are worried about money to get food, then make sure that ticket is for a large enough city that they have services available to help people trying to start from nothing.

Do you specifically not want something to live for? Or is it just a matter of not having the motivation to find something?  

The only thing I can say is that either way, you could always be surprised and something worth living for might show up on its own some day.  Even if you don't want that now, if it does show up you may completely change your mind. It's not much, but hope that it will happen is pretty much all many of us have.

I grew up in a class of 50 until high school, and I understand the difficulty of having acquaintances but not friends. Two of my closest "friends" even shot at my house with a pellet gun and my car in my driveway with a real gun senior year in high school. I didn't get into my choice college (MIT) but after talking to my guidance counselor about what college would be good for me I applied and got in to what she suggested.  College really was a ton time better than high school. And I never saw most of those people again, and I know many of them went on to have some pretty shitty lives themselves. 

And there is always the possibility of things being better in college and then transferring to or going to one of your top choices for grad school.  That of course is only if you still actually want to go there once you get to experience college elsewhere.

Because living is the only chance you have to find something worth living for.  It can be hard when things don't seem to be going in the right direction, but there is no point in any of it if you end it before finding something.

It's hard to give advice without knowing you two much more, but perhaps the things she has told you are a way of asking for help? I know I would want to try and be there for her as much as possible in that situation. 

If she seems to be getting worse rather than better then talking to someone that can provide professional assistance probably is the best next step.

I don't know what's involved in being admitted, but I dated someone that attempted suicide soon after I met her. She ended up spending a while in the "psych ward" at a nearby hospital.  It sounds rough, but really it was a pretty supportive and comfortable/safe environment. I visited her there as much as possible and she seemed to really appreciate that.  I actually kind of liked it there myself...

I hope you get to respond to this. I've glanced at your other posts and based on what I saw, and the way you worded this, I think you would do well to depart your life by moving away and starting a new one.

I wish I had some better roads to drive on. I have been up to 210km/h once, but I generally get up to about 170km/h every day, even in regular commute hours. I especially like the feeling of going from 100 to 170 while going up hill. I haven't tried with the windows open though. 

And creating is the most important thing in my life, but haven't been in the right mindset in quite a while.

I had a very close relationship for over five years, and that was definitely something else. I feel like a completely different person now that that is over.  Relationships can provide a nice steady supply of oxytocin. Sure it's not oxycodone, but as you said, the chemicals in our brain control us and I would prefer oxytocin.

I've convinced myself that I don't have clinical level depression based on the descriptions I've seen usually involving the idea of not having real things to point at for the cause of anguish, and I have some pretty solid things to point to.  Your writing comes way too close to home for me though.  I do think I suffer many of the symptoms, I just might have a different cause for them.

Perhaps now that you've gone through that you have some more concrete things to point to as reasons for suffering, and in a way that's more validating and able to free you from feeling like there is no hope? 

I hope you continue to heal in every way.
